title: Window: PARTITION BY
story: PARTITION BY restarts the window for each group. Find the priciest product per category.
goal: Show the most expensive product in each category: columns category, name, price, ordered by category.

tests.label: Hidden check on other data

hints: OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) numbers each category from 1.
Keep rn = 1 in an outer query. Add ORDER BY category.
SELECT category, name, price FROM (SELECT category, name, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn FROM products) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY category;
socratic: Why can't WHERE rn = 1 be in the same SELECT?
What would RANK do on a tie?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the PARTITION BY?
solution: SELECT category, name, price FROM (SELECT category, name, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn FROM products) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY category;
alt: SELECT category, name, price FROM (SELECT category, name, price, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS r FROM products) WHERE r = 1 ORDER BY category;
